title: 2003 HMMT February Guts Problem 10
statement: Suppose that \(A, B, C, D\) are four points in the plane, and let \(Q, R, S, T, U, V\) be the respective midpoints of \(A B, A C, A D, B C, B D, C D\). If \(Q R=2001, S U=2002, T V=\) 2003, find the distance between the midpoints of \(Q U\) and \(R V\).

solutions.text:
2001

This problem has far more information than necessary: \(Q R\) and \(U V\) are both parallel to \(B C\), and \(Q U\) and \(R V\) are both parallel to \(A D\). Hence, \(Q U V R\) is a parallelogram, and the desired distance is simply the same as the side length \(Q R\), namely 2001. (See figure, next page.)
